analysis.evidence: In הֲלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ לְפָנֶיךָ, “Is not the whole land before you?”, כָל refers to the full extent of the land available to Lot as he chooses left or right.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, with הָאָרֶץ as its complement.

analysis.evidence: Abram asks Lot whether the whole land lies before him (כָל הָאָרֶץ לְפָנֶיךָ). His offer to go right if Lot goes left, or left if Lot goes right, identifies the land as the territory available to them.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes אָרֶץ, a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute. The noun takes the form אָרֶץ with the article.

analysis.evidence: Abram asks Lot whether the whole land lies before him. The choice between left and right makes the spatial sense explicit.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ combines with the plural construct of פָּנִים, a noun of both genders, and the second-person masculine singular suffix ךָ referring to Lot. Together they function as a preposition with a pronominal object.

draft.change: Add the sense ‘part company’ to the Niphal of פָּרַד.
draft.definition: To part company with someone by going one's own way.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 13:9 Abram asks Lot to separate from him and offers to go in whichever direction Lot leaves open.

analysis.evidence: Abram specifies מֵעָלָי, ‘from me,’ and offers Lot a choice of directions. If Lot goes left, Abram will go right, and if Lot goes right, Abram will go left.
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperative, second person masculine singular, addressed to Lot. The initial הִ and the doubling of פ mark the Niphal form. The following נָא softens the request and is a separate word.

analysis.evidence: נָא follows the masculine singular imperative הִפָּרֶד and softens Abram’s request to Lot in הִפָּרֶד נָא מֵעָלָי, ‘Please part from me.’
analysis.morphology: Hebrew particle of entreaty, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Abram asks Lot הִפָּרֶד נָא מֵעָלָי ‘please separate from me’. The alternatives of going left or right show that Lot is to leave Abram’s side. עַל expresses proximity here, and מֵ־ marks movement away.
analysis.morphology: The prefix מֵ־ is a form of מִן ‘from’. It precedes the preposition עַל, which bears the first-person singular suffix ‘me’.

analysis.evidence: אִם הַשְּׂמֹאל means “if you go left,” with the verb of motion understood. Abram gives the consequence in וְאֵימִנָה, “then I will go right.”
analysis.morphology: Unprefixed Hebrew conjunction with no suffix.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew noun שְׂמֹאל with its directional sense.
draft.definition: The left side, opposed to the right, especially as a direction one may take.
draft.evidence: In Gen.13.9 the two conditional clauses exchange left and right as Lot’s and Abram’s respective directions.

analysis.evidence: Abram offers Lot a choice of land. If Lot takes הַשְּׂמֹאל, Abram will go right. The next clause reverses the choice, pairing הַיָּמִין, “the right,” with Abram going left.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial שׂ of the masculine singular absolute noun. After אִם, the noun names the side Lot may choose. The verb of motion is understood.
analysis.sense: The left side as a direction of travel.

analysis.evidence: Abram tells Lot that if Lot takes the left (אִם הַשְּׂמֹאל), Abram will go to the right (וְאֵימִנָה). The next clause reverses the directions.
analysis.gloss: then I will go to the right
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces the result of the condition. אֵימִנָה is a Hiphil first-person common singular cohortative expressing the speaker’s intention.
analysis.sense: go or turn to the right

analysis.evidence: Abram sets הַיָּמִין opposite הַשְּׂמֹאל as the two directions Lot can choose. The following וְאַשְׂמְאִילָה supplies the contrast: if Lot goes right, Abram will go left.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a feminine singular absolute noun and doubles its initial י.
analysis.sense: to the right (in turning); right or left

draft.change: Append the directional verb שָׂמַאל to the article for שׂמאל.
draft.definition: In the Hiphil, to go to the left.
draft.evidence: In Gen.13.9 Abram says וְאַשְׂמְאִילָה if Lot takes the right, reversing his offer to go right if Lot takes the left.

analysis.evidence: Abram first offers to go right if Lot chooses the left. The second clause reverses the directions: וְאִם הַיָּמִין gives Lot the choice of the right, and וְאַשְׂמְאִילָה expresses Abram’s resolve to go left.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces Abram’s response to Lot’s possible choice. אַשְׂמְאִילָה is a Hiphil first-person common singular cohortative. The א prefix marks the speaker, and the final ־ָה marks his resolve.
